haiku-low.q1: Step 1 reads row_count from the replica. At 10,000 rows or fewer, the CSV downloads directly (200, text/csv). Above that, a background job runs and the user gets 202 JSON plus a status panel.
haiku-low.q2: The duplicate click gets 202 with the active export's ID, state, filters and cols. A different-filters click (message or 409) is an open question.
haiku-low.q3: The emailed link lasts the smaller of 24 hours and expires_at minus now, so 24 hours. The bucket keeps files 7 days. The document does not say what removes them.
haiku-low.q4: Up to 3 attempts, retried after 60 and 300 seconds. After the last failure the row is marked failed, the upload is aborted, and an export_failed email is sent. The page shows Export failed with the error.
haiku-low.q5: The replica, a read-only copy of the database. Writes go to the primary.
haiku-low.q6: In the report_exports row on the primary. The page polls the latest-export endpoint every 3 seconds while queued or running. Reopening shows the same status. No browser storage is used.
haiku-low.q7: It reads 5,000-row pages from the replica by row_id, formats them into an 8 MiB buffer, and uploads each as a multipart part. It never holds the whole report, only about 2 MB at a time.
haiku-low.q8: Recorded parts stay in storage 24 hours. The checkpoint (upload_id, parts, last_row_id) is kept, and the next attempt resumes from last_row_id, re-uploading any unrecorded part. No rows are lost.
haiku-low.q9: They are stored in the report_exports row (filters and cols) at insert time. The job payload holds only export_id, so the job reads filters and cols from the row.
haiku-low.q10: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where state is queued or running. The second insert is rejected, and the request returns the existing active export.
haiku-low.q11: The file must be done, with object_key set and the object at exports/<export_id>.csv. If emailed_at is empty, the job sends the email only, with no lease. If emailed_at is set, it returns normally.
haiku-low.q12: The whole file is built in memory before any byte is sent, so no partial file reaches the user. A replica error or 60-second limit gives 503, Export failed, try again. Retry is safe because nothing was stored.

sonnet.q1: Chosen by reports.row_count read from the replica: 10,000 or fewer goes the small path, above 10,000 the large path. Small: a 200 text/csv file download straight from the click, built fully in memory. Large: a 202 JSON (export_id, state, filters, cols), the page shows a status panel, the job writes the file to the exports bucket and emails a 24-hour download link.
sonnet.q2: The partial unique index rejects the insert, so no new export is created. The server returns 202 with the existing active export's ID, state, filters and cols, so the page shows what that export covers. (Whether to message or return 409 for different filters is an open question.)
sonnet.q3: The link works 24 hours (signed URL lifetime is the smaller of 24 hours and expires_at minus now; expires_at = completion + 24h). The bucket's lifecycle rule keeps files 7 days (the doc says the bucket keeps files for 7 days); the lifecycle rule also removes leftover parts of aborted uploads after 24 hours. Rows are never deleted; no cleanup job.
sonnet.q4: Up to 3 attempts. After attempt 3 fails the final-failure handler sets state failed with an error summary, aborts the upload if upload_id is set, and sends the export_failed email. The page shows "Export failed: <error>" with a Try again button. (If the row was already done, it is not marked failed; it is logged and operators alerted, and the user still sees Download.)
sonnet.q5: The replica (read-only copy). Writes go to the primary.
sonnet.q6: In the report_exports row on the primary (state, attempt, error, expires_at, heartbeat etc.). The page polls GET /api/reports/{id}/exports/latest every 3 seconds while queued or running, and loads it on page load, so reopening later (even on another device) shows the same status. Nothing is kept in the browser.
sonnet.q7: It streams in parts: reads 5,000-row pages from the replica, formats into an 8 MiB in-memory buffer, uploads each as a multipart part (about 115 parts), so a worker holds only one 8 MiB buffer and one ~2 MB page and never the whole report. The doc does not mention a 512 MB worker specifically; memory use is about 10 MiB of buffers.
sonnet.q8: Data already uploaded as parts stays in storage under the same multipart upload (nothing visible at the final key). The checkpoint (upload_id, parts, last_row_id) is saved on the row. The next attempt resumes from last_row_id with the same upload_id. A part that failed to upload and was not recorded is re-read from last_row_id and uploaded again. After a dead worker the row becomes stale (heartbeat over 5 min) and the queue retries from the checkpoint.
sonnet.q9: They are stored in the filters and cols columns of the report_exports row, inserted at click time. The job payload holds only the export_id, and the job loads the row to get them.
sonnet.q10: The database's partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) where state is queued or running; the loser's insert is rejected and it returns the existing active export.
sonnet.q11: The file must be complete: the multipart upload completed and the row recorded as done (with object_key, expires_at). On a rerun: if the row is missing, failed, or done with emailed_at set, the job returns normally doing nothing. If done with emailed_at empty, it skips rebuilding and goes straight to Step 7 (send the email, set emailed_at) without needing a lease.
sonnet.q12: The server returns 503 (replica error or the 60-second API limit), no bytes of a partial file are sent because the file is built fully in memory first, nothing is stored, and the page shows "Export failed, try again." Retrying is safe.
